articles.title: Eclipse over South Africa
articles.summary: Ernie Piini recounts his expedition to South Africa for a total solar eclipse, where despite meticulous planning and a clear night sky, clouds unfortunately obscured much of the 1 minute and 24 second totality near Messina. The trip, part of Jen Winter's Astronomical Tours, also included an extensive travelogue featuring a three-day safari through Kruger National Park and visits to various scenic and historic sites.

articles.title: Sic transit mundi
articles.summary: This article delves into Transient Lunar Phenomena (TLP), categorizing them from verifiable optical effects like lunar rays to unconfirmed or highly improbable events. The author explains that many reported "changes" on the Moon are likely due to unique lighting conditions and terrain rather than actual alterations. While expressing interest in witnessing a significant impact event, the article emphasizes a skeptical approach to sensational claims, noting that observers often perceive what they desire to see.

articles.title: Observing Reports: So Little Time, So Much to See!
articles.summary: This article encourages deep-sky observers to seize the fleeting "galaxy season" despite challenging weather and diminishing dark hours. It provides a curated list of specific deep-sky targets, predominantly galaxies but also a planetary nebula, located in constellations such as Hydra, Corvus, Leo, and Ursa Major. Each entry includes detailed observing notes and anecdotal reports from experienced astronomers, encouraging readers to actively explore these celestial wonders before the season ends.

articles.title: Change of date for the April SJAA General meeting.
articles.summary: The April SJAA General meeting date has been changed to Sunday, April 13, 2003, at 7:00 p.m. due to a scheduling conflict with speaker Dr. Fulvio Melia. The meeting, which follows the SJAA Auction, will feature Dr. Melia discussing 'The Black Hole at the Center of Our Galaxy'. There is a possibility of a 'Dinner with the Speaker' before the talk.

articles.title: SJAA Yosemite public star party, 2003
articles.summary: The annual SJAA Yosemite public star party is scheduled for July 25 and 26, 2003, at Glacier Point in Yosemite National Park. Up to 30 participants will receive free admission and camping in exchange for hosting public stargazing events, with an expectation of at least one telescope per two people. The article provides details on reservations, contact information, and an editor's note regarding the limitations of the group campsite.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series Wednesday, April 23, 7 p.m.
articles.summary: Dr. Scott Sanford of NASA Ames will deliver a non-technical, illustrated talk on the Stardust mission as part of the free Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series on Wednesday, April 23, at Foothill College. The lecture will detail the mission's goal of returning comet samples to Earth, providing humanity with its first opportunity to study the original material from which our solar system was built.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article details the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, available exclusively to its members. It provides lists of telescopes available for immediate loan, those currently borrowed (including due dates), and scopes with extended loan periods, along with a waiting list. Members interested in borrowing a scope or inquiring about availability are directed to contact Mike Koop.
